results.comment: Perhaps the most beautiful and underrated aspect of this second appearance by Randall Carlson is how thoughtfully crafted each discussion is. Clearly this man is a brilliant educator, because he says something at the 1:16:00 mark that almost blew right past me. He's demonstrating to Joe what the Bering Land Bridge looked like and in the process mentions Atlantis, but rather than draw that out into a separate discussion he just goes; "We talked about that last time, but... ".  I know this seems like a minor thing, but one of the issues I have with repeat guests on podcasts is that they almost always come with repeat stories. If you listen to both episodes with Paul Stamets, for example, you'll very quickly realize that these are basically the same episode repeated over two separate appearances. Whether this is because the guest is unsure what he's already told Joe or because he really only has a podcast's worth of information to his name, we may never know. What we do know, though, is that for any listeners paying serious attention to these episodes (which many do) these rehashed conversations can be incredibly wearing.  No disrespect to Graham Hancock, because he's one of my absolute favorite guests, but even he is guilty of repeating certain stories or nuggets of information every single time he appears on the podcast. What I'm noticing from Randall Carlson, though, is that his first two appearances are not only entirely different, but the second is an almost perfect compliment to the first. It makes me wonder if Randall didn't listen to his first appearance before recording his second just to avoid repeating himself, because his knowledge of what had already been said is practically flawless.  Not only does this make him an excellent guest and friend to Joe Rogan, but it makes him a truly special educator. That kind of attention to detail is rare, and it only enhances his credibility as a scientist to have so much of this subject in order. This is clearly a man who cares very much about his work and it shows a great deal of integrity that he comes so prepared. It's because he's this disciplined that he's able to make such a complicated subject so easy to understand. In my opinion, that really is the mark of a true genius. I suppose that's why this video is nearing the 10 million views mark and counting.   And credit to Joe for giving him such a platform! His ability to just sit and listen, and only chime in when there's a pertinent question to be asked, absolutely contributes to the specialness of these episodes. He really does do a brilliant job making Randall look good. When it comes to podcast hosts, from a listener's perspective, that's all you can ask for!
